 And
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Police
 Station Kotwali Anuppur (Madhya Pradesh)
 
 (By Ms. Shweta Yadav, Govt. Advocate)

This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER 1.

This is first bail application filed under Section 439 CrPC on behalf of applicant who is in custody since 25.2.2023 in connection with Crime No.461/2022 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Annuppur (M.P.), for the offence punishable under sections 376, 376(2)(n), 354D, 450 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 66E of I.T Act.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that prosecutrix was major and is a consenting party.
She has lodged false F.I.R against the applicant.
In these circumstances, applicant may be enlarged on bail.
3. Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the respondent/State opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
It is submitted by him that applicant used to pester the prosecutrix, therefore, she has changed residence.
Applicant again came to her house and committed act repeatedly.

In these circumstances Mohanlal Tandiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128024211/

sentences.text: he may not be released on bail.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
5. There is delay in lodging of F.I.R. Prosecutrix, even after being teased and harassed by applicant,
agreed to make food for the applicant and thereafter she is said to have been raped by applicant but there was delay in lodging of F.I.R.
6.
Considering the aforesaid circumstances, bail application filed by the applicant is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for his appearance before the trial court on the dates to be fixed by the trial court.

8. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
C.C as per rules.
